html:
The Chesepians were an Algonquian people who lived on the south shore of the mouth of Chesapeake Bay, around today's Norfolk and Virginia Beach. The bay takes its name from them.

The English first met them in 1585 and 1586, when men from the Roanoke colony spent a winter in their country. Twenty years later they were gone. The paramount chief Powhatan, whose realm covered most of coastal Virginia, told the English that he had destroyed them, reportedly because his priests had warned that a people from the bay would overthrow him. This happened about the time Jamestown was founded in 1607, and historians still argue over the details. Their neighbours across the James River were the Quiyoughcohannock.
sum: The Chesepians were an Algonquian people who lived on the south shore of the mouth of Chesapeake Bay, around today's Norfolk and Virginia Beach. The bay takes its name from them.
